sections.h2: Where is the Leelanau County Register of Deeds?
sections.html:
The office is at 8527 E. Government Center Drive, Suite 105, in Suttons Bay, and its phone number is 231-256-9682. Email goes to rod@leelanau.gov. The county seat moved from Leland to a site in Suttons Bay Township in 2008.

The Register of Deeds is a constitutional office that dates to Michigan's first constitution in 1835, and Leelanau County has had fifteen registers since 1863. Records go back to that year. Documents received after 4:30 p.m. are held until the next business day, so a deed dropped off late in the afternoon waits for the next business day.

The office records instruments that transfer or encumber real property, and it cannot judge whether a document is legally sufficient or what its author intended. Michigan is a race-notice state, so papers are recorded in the order they are first presented, and first in time is first in line.

sections.h2: What is Leelanau County like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Leelanau County is the entire Leelanau Peninsula, a triangle of land about 30 miles long that reaches into Lake Michigan from the western Lower Peninsula and is about 25 miles wide at its base. The county's total area is 2,532 square miles, but only 347 of them are land, because 86% of the area is water.

It has the second highest share of water of any county in the country. Lake Leelanau is the largest inland lake, Glen Lake lies inside the Sleeping Bear Dunes National Lakeshore, and North and South Manitou Islands lie within the county line. Part of Traverse City falls inside Leelanau, and Elmwood Charter Township, on the southeastern edge, is the most urbanized piece. The villages are Empire, Northport and Suttons Bay, and ten civil townships cover the rest, including Leland, Glen Arbor, Solon and Centerville. The 2020 census counted 22,301 people, up from 21,708 in 2010.

Leelanau became its own organized county in 1863 and touches other Michigan counties by land only at Grand Traverse and Benzie. Sleeping Bear Dunes National Lakeshore was established in 1970. The Grand Traverse Band of Ottawa and Chippewa Indians occupies scattered areas within Suttons Bay Township. Every deed for any of this ground is filed in the Suttons Bay office.

sections.h2: What makes a deed recordable in Leelanau County?
sections.html:
The office accepts only documents with original signatures, and it does not allow digital recording. It has kept the wet ink requirement on purpose, because it has stopped fraud attempts that way.

  • A court document must be certified by the court. A true copy cannot be recorded, and the same applies to a death certificate.
  • Under MCL 565.201 each signer's name is printed, typed or stamped beneath the signature, and the signature is in black or dark blue ink.
  • The notary's name appears on the same page near the signature.
  • Each grantee's street address, or post office address, appears on a deed.
  • The drafter's name and business address appear on instruments signed after January 1, 1964.

The office does not supply forms or give legal help. For drafting it points people to an attorney or title company, and it does not run title searches.

sections.h2: What does recording cost in Leelanau County?
sections.html:
State law sets recording at $30 for any document, whatever its length, and the office accepts cash, checks, debit cards and credit cards. One check can cover recording for several documents, along with transfer tax, a tax certificate and any copy fees.

sections.h2: How is transfer tax figured in Leelanau County?
sections.html:
The county rate is 55 cents for each $500 of value, and the state rate is $3.75 for each $500, with any fraction of $500 counted as a full unit. On a $400,000 sale that is $440 to the county and $3,000 to the state, or $3,440. The seller owes it, and it is paid at the Register of Deeds.

Leelanau's own guidance adds several points. The instrument must state the total consideration on its face, and a Real Estate Transfer Valuation Affidavit can be filed instead, at no charge, if the deed says one is being filed. Property in more than one county needs the sale price split by parcel, with tax paid to each county. Documentary stamps are bought only in the county where the land lies. An easement is taxable, and a foreclosure instrument carries county tax based on the stated sale price.

Exemptions listed in MCL 207.505 include transfers for under $100, instruments given as security, leases, land contracts that have not yet passed title, spousal conveyances creating a tenancy by the entireties and corrective quitclaims.

sections.h2: How do I search Leelanau County land records?
sections.html:
Use the county's Self Service site, the two public workstations in the Suttons Bay office, or the vault. Names go in last name first with no punctuation, and the search needs a grantor or grantee name plus an approximate year.

  • The free search shows index information only, and each image costs $1.00 per page.
  • Subscription passes run $5 for 15 minutes, $15 for a day, $200 a month and $1,100 for six months.
  • A parcel number search requires the county prefix 45 and the dashes, as in 45-000-000-000-00, and only documents that list the number turn up.
  • Online, only deed records are available before January 1, 1972. Other older records are searched in the office.
  • The historical grantor and grantee indexes went online in October 2025.

Try spelling variants, such as Richard, Rick and Dick, because the office records names exactly as written on each document.

sections.h2: What happens to the record after a payoff, a death or a sheriff's sale?
sections.html:
The office only records, so it does not issue a replacement deed after any of these events. Your original deed stays the deed to the property.

  • After a mortgage payoff, the lender sends a discharge or satisfaction of mortgage. No new deed follows, because the deed was delivered when you bought.
  • When a co-owner dies, bring a certified death certificate and the recording fee. It shows that the deceased person no longer holds an interest.
  • A sheriff's deed is recorded when it is submitted after the auction closes. The office is not the place to redeem; the attorney named on the sheriff's deed handles that.
  • If you have lost your deed, a recorded copy is available at the office, and copy fees apply.

sections.h2: How can Leelanau County owners watch for property fraud?
sections.html:
Subscribe to Fraud Notify, which is free. It emails you when a document is recorded under a name you register, and the office has reported several attempts to list owners' property fraudulently that were stopped once owners were told.

If you see a neighbor's lot offered for sale, ask the owner. The office also warns about mail that looks official and charges for copies of your own deed. A 2016 Michigan law set rules for such mailings, and a copy from the office is $1.00 a page.

faqs.q: What is the phone number for the Leelanau County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: 231-256-9682. The office is in Suttons Bay at 8527 E. Government Center Drive, Suite 105, and also takes questions by email at rod@leelanau.gov.

faqs.q: Does Leelanau County record deeds electronically?
faqs.a: No. The office requires original wet ink signatures and does not allow digital recording, to make deed fraud harder.

faqs.q: How much is transfer tax on a Leelanau County sale?
faqs.a: Together 55 cents plus $3.75 for each $500 of value, so $4.30 per $500. The seller pays at the Register of Deeds.

faqs.q: Can I record a copy of a death certificate in Leelanau County?
faqs.a: Only a certified one. The office will not record a true copy, and it does not issue a new deed afterward, because it only records.

faqs.q: How do I get a copy of my deed in Leelanau County?
faqs.a: Visit the Suttons Bay office, call 231-256-9682 or use the Self Service website. Copies are $1.00 per page.
